long_biography.plain_text:
Shipyard owner Vitaly Yusufov chose to keep the Wismar and Warnemünde sites together when bidding for their insolvent predecessor. His offer committed to preserving jobs and repaying debts. He then sought work beyond conventional shipbuilding, winning orders from Siemens for converter platforms serving offshore wind farms.

The Arctic rescue vessels Murman and Beringov Proliv required a different kind of coordination. Yusufov described bringing German shipyard expertise together with Russian rescue and navigation equipment, outfitters and specialist suppliers. Fitting these systems into limited space was a central engineering challenge for vessels intended to operate in icebound waters.
